A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RANGE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary sections are readable and support comparison, including the additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream-task evaluations, iNaturalist results, retrieval ablations, checkerboard experiments, and ERA5 regression results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds image-only results, training-free iNaturalist comparisons, and computational timings.

M1.justification: The SatCLIP/SatMAE feature database, semantic softmax retrieval, spatial retrieval, beta-weighted combination, and embedding concatenation remain unchanged. The added training sentence in Section 4.1 clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same geospatial tasks, iNaturalist 2018, ERA5 variables, and synthetic checkerboard scenarios. The new baseline comparisons reuse existing tasks; the timing report changes hardware and workload settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 7 adds Direct, Cartesian, Wrap, SphereC+, and SphereM+ to the iNaturalist comparison. These encodings already appeared in the downstream-task comparison, but their geoprior evaluation is new. Table 1 also adds a SatMAE-only diagnostic comparator.

E3.justification: Section 13 introduces a timing evaluation using a 10,000-entry database and one million query locations on CPU and H100 GPU. Previously reported probing procedures, hyperparameters, database-size experiments, and checkerboard settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds an image-only control to the existing location-versus-combined-feature analysis, and Section 13 adds computational-cost evidence. The database-size, retrieval-selection, temperature, beta-sensitivity, and embedding-visualization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. The revised database-size plot adds no uncertainty reporting, and the new runtime statements provide no repetition or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds SatMAE scores of 58.8, 28.4, 0.388, and 0.600. Table 7 adds training-free iNaturalist scores, including SphereM+ top-1 accuracy of 70.8%, alongside unchanged RANGE scores. Section 13 reports runtimes below 65 seconds on CPU and 10 seconds on H100. Existing Tables 2–6 and database-size curves retain their results.

T1.justification: The multiview non-redundancy argument and Equations 1–7 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about recovering visual information through retrieval, controlling spatial smoothness, and providing efficient multi-resolution embeddings. The headline gains of 13.1% and 0.145 R2 are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 13 newly explains practical efficiency through one-time feature-bank construction and vectorized retrieval, while acknowledging retrieval overhead. The California-housing temporal-mismatch interpretation and satellite-imagery applicability limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces generic future GitHub/HuggingFace release statements with a named RANGE repository for code and models, without establishing actual release availability. Section 13 adds vectorization, feature-bank construction, workload, and H100 hardware information. Section 8's implementation settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. SatCLIP's reference changes from its arXiv entry to AAAI 2025 publication details, representing the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes light wording and author-header edits, adds main-text pointers to existing supplementary experiments, and introduces two short supplementary sections. The unchanged limitations section moves from Section 12 to Section 14; the main narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 receive graphical cleanup, including clearer labels and a reorganized legend in Figure 3. Table 1 gains a row, Table 3 abbreviates its temperature heading, and Table 7 is added. Other figures and table structures are retained, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The image-only control in Table 1 and training-free comparisons in Table 7 fill modest comparison gaps. Section 13 gives quantitative support for practical efficiency, while the repository pointer and clearer figures improve usability. These additions strengthen the paper without changing its core study, although the timing evidence remains limited by unspecified CPU hardware and absent repetition or uncertainty information.
